newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jinro Group units fall on liquidity fear.
newsitem.headline: Jinro Group units fall on liquidity fear.

text.p: Four listed shares of South Korea's Jinro Group fell sharply on Friday on market talks that the companies were suffering from liquidity problem, brokers said.
The Jinro Group denied the rumours. "The rumours that we are experiencing serious financial problems are totally groundless," director Kim Young-jin told Reuters.
Four companies belonging to the Jinro Group are listed on the Seoul bourse.
Jinro Ltd, a leading distilled spirit producer, went limit down to 10,700, a fall of 900 won.
Jinro Industries and Jinro General Foods both fell to their daily limits to 5,410 won and 5,390 won, shedding 470 won and 460 won respectively. Kumbi, a glass bottle maker, lost 2,900 won to 33,500.
Brokers said the Jinro Group was rumoured to be facing liquidity problems after its unlisted affiliate had trouble paying a debt obligation on Thursday.
Kim said the company did delay paying two billion won worth of promissory notes. "It was a procedural error. I believe the market distorted the error," he said.
A Korea Stock Exchange official said the bourse asked Jinro Group to clarify the market rumours.
